 Live Updates Updated Tue, Nov 3 2026 10:31 PM EST Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Midterm elections 2026 live updates: Democrats projected to win House, poised to take Senate
 Justin Papp Caleigh Keating Garrett Downs Kevin Breuninger Dan Mangan This is CNBC's live coverage of the 2026 midterm elections. 
 Democrats are projected to have a commanding majority in the U.S. House, surging past the 218 seats needed to control the chamber, according to a CNBC Election Desk projection. The desk projects Democrats will win at least 235 seats in the chamber. And the party is now leaning toward flipping four Republican-controlled Senate seats — in Kansas, Ohio, Texas and South Carolina, the desk projects.
 The key midterm election is deciding control of Congress and will define President Donald Trump 's final years in office.
 Democrats already flipped the North Carolina Senate seat with a victory by former Gov. Roy Cooper.
 The Associated Press provides vote data and race projections for CNBC. Polls began closing at 6 p.m. ET, and Alaska will be the last to close at 1 a.m. ET. 
 What to know 
 Follow House results: Map 
 Democrats projected to win control of the House 
 Texas Senate seat "leans" D 
 Roy Cooper flips North Carolina Senate seat 
 Ossoff wins Georgia Senate race 
 Florida Senate seat "leaning Republican" 
 3 Min Ago Alex Soros celebrates Democrats' early wins
 Open Society Foundations Chairman Alex Soros has taken to X to celebrate the reported positive projections for Democrats.
 "This is like the Mets, Jets, and Knicks all winning in the same year," Soros wrote online . "If we win Alaska you can throw in St. John's!" 
 Soros has a long history of supporting the Democratic Party along with his father, George Soros. The two donated $102 million to their super PAC, called Democracy PAC, this election cycle. 
 — Irit Skulnik 
 16 Min Ago White House mood 'defiant' in face of projected Democratic wins
 President Donald Trump listens to a reporter's question in the Oval Office at the White House, in Washington, Sept. 28, 2026. Kevin Dietsch | Getty Images The mood in the White House in the face of what is shaping up to be a Democratic electoral wave "is defiant," a White House official said, speaking on the condition of anonymity.
 "President Trump was not on the ballot, and it's proven that Trump voters show up when he is on the ballot," the official said.
 "Also, candidate quality matters, and President Trump did a better job promoting many of the candidates on the ballot than the candidates did themselves."
 The official argued that voters who cast ballots for Democrats who won their races "are going to have a serious case of [buyer's] remorse when gas prices come down quickly when the Iran conflict is solved but they're still stuck with a list of liberal extremist Democrats."
 "And a final note here: regardless of how today plays out, President Trump's resolve to stop the Radical Left is only going to become stronger. Buckle up."
 — Dan Mangan 
 18 Min Ago CNBC Election Desk moves Kansas Senate race to 'leans Democratic'
 Adam Hamilton, Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate for Kansas, speaks to voters outside the Kansas Oil Museum in El Dorado, Kansas, Oct. 29, 2026. Austin Johnson | AFP | Getty Images The CNBC Election Desk has moved Kansas' Senate race to "leans Democratic," as Republican Sen. Roger Marshall faces a challenge from Democrat Adam Hamilton, a United Methodist pastor. The race has become an unexpected battleground in a state that has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1932. 
 — Luke Fountain 
 23 Min Ago Darline Graham viewed as too inexperienced in quest for brother's seat
 U.S. Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., speaks at a campaign event at Holt Bros BBQ in Florence, South Carolina, on Aug. 19, 2026. Sean Rayford | Getty Images Darline Graham struggled to keep her brother's South Carolina Senate seat amid questions over her experience.
 Just 37% of respondents to the CNBC Voter Poll thought the Republican had the experience to carry on the legacy of her brother, Lindsay Graham , who died in July. Voters were split on Democrat Annie Andrews, with 48% saying her views were too extreme and 51% saying the opposite.
 Graham was appointed to the seat following her brother's death.
 — Jeff Cox 
 25 Min Ago Voters see corruption as a big issue, differ on which party can address it
 People walk near the U.S. Capitol in Washington, May 21, 2026. Aaron Schwartz | Bloomberg | Getty Images Voters nationwide placed a high priority on fighting corruption in Tuesday's elections but were less convinced about which party was better at handling the issue.
 In the CNBC Voter Poll, 90% of respondents said the issue was either crucial or a major factor when evaluating candidates. 
 However, when asked which party was better at addressing corruption, Democrats had a 36% to 31% advantage — with 33% saying "neither."
 — Jeff Cox 
 31 Min Ago Democrats will take control of House, CNBC Election Desk projects
 Democrats will take majority control of the U.S. House, CNBC's Election Desk projects.
 The party is poised to win a minimum of 225 House seats when all races are complete, versus a minimum of 160 seats for Republicans, the desk projects. A party needs at least 218 seats to control the chamber.
 — Kevin Breuninger 
 31 Min Ago Democrat Hamilton shows strength in deep-red Kansas Senate race
 Incumbent U.S. Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kansas, at left, and Adam Hamilton, Democratic Senate candidate for Kansas. Getty Images Democrat Adam Hamilton is threatening a historic upset in deep-red Kansas, leading Republican Sen. Roger Marshall by double digits in a key county Trump won handily in 2024, with significant votes still outstanding in populous areas.
 With 70% of votes counted in Sedgwick County, home to Wichita, Hamilton leads 55% to 42.8% — a sharp reversal from Trump's nearly 14-point victory there in 2024. The county is a major aerospace manufacturing hub where Trump's trade policies have threatened local jobs .
 Significant votes remain outstanding in some of Kansas' most populous areas, where Hamilton is likely to be strongest, particularly as Democrats gain momentum nationwide.
 — Luke Fountain 
 32 Min Ago Democrat Rebecca Bennett defeats Republican Rep. Tom Kean in key House flip
 Rebecca Bennett, Democratic U.S. House candidate for New Jersey, during a primary election night event in Bridgewater, New Jersey, June 2, 2026. Adam Gray | Bloomberg | Getty Images Democrat Rebecca Bennett has defeated Republican Rep. Tom Kean in a key House flip, the AP projected. 
 Bennett, a former Navy helicopter pilot, defeated the embattled congressman after mental health challenges sidelined him for months during the last Congress. 
 Kean did not disclose the reason for his absence until he returned, prompting rampant speculation about his whereabouts. 
 — Garrett Downs 
 35 Min Ago U.S. stock futures slide as traders brace for potential Democratic sweep in midterm elections
 Stock futures dropped as traders speculated that Democrats were headed for majority control of Congress and some key gubernatorial wins in the 2026 U.S. midterm elections .
 Futures tied to the S&P 500 traded 1.1% lower, while Nasdaq-100 futures shed 2%. Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average were down 367 points, or 0.7%.
 If Democrats are able to secure a sizable majority in the Senate — the so-called blue-wave scenario —  the market and especially stocks related to the artificial intelligence buildout could come under pressure, according to some on Wall Street. Investors fear a big Democratic win could mean more restrictions on data centers nationwide. 
 AI-linked stocks have already pulled back in recent weeks on concern about a slowing pace in data center-related spending.
 — Sean Conlon, Lee Ying Shan 
 41 Min Ago Early Mississippi returns hint at trouble for Republicans as Democrats gain ground across South
 A voter fills out his ballot at a polling location at Jackson State University on Election Day, Nov. 3, 2026 in Jackson, Mississippi. Azariah Wells | Jackson State University | Getty Images Mississippi could be the next test of Democrats' momentum across the South, with early returns hinting at potential trouble for Republicans in traditionally safe territory. Jasper County, a predominantly Black rural county and among the first to finish tallying ballots, moved about 19 percentage points toward Democrats relative to the 2024 presidential race. It's just one county, but a comparable shift in other counties across the state could turn an otherwise lopsided contest into a competitive one.
 — Luke Fountain 
 45 Min Ago Whatley's Senate loss comes amid views he was too close to Trump
 Michael Whatley, former chair of the Republican National Committee and Republican U.S. Senate candidate for North Carolina, during an election night event in Gastonia, North Carolina, Nov. 3, 2026. Cornell Watson | Bloomberg | Getty Images Count Michael Whatley among the Republicans voters may have eschewed for supporting Trump.
 Whatley is projected to come up short, according to the AP, in his quest for a North Carolina Senate seat, with 58% in the CNBC Voter Poll saying the Republican was too close to Trump. In addition, Whatley was 14 points underwater in favorability, with just 36% of respondents viewing him positively.
 — Jeff Cox 
 46 Min Ago Jewish voters largely support Democrats despite Israel debates
 Support for Democrats among Jewish voters held steady, even as U.S. aid for Israel became a hot-button issue on the campaign trail, according to the CNBC Voter Poll.
 Jewish-identifying voters backed Democratic House candidates by a margin of 34 percentage points in 2026. Of these voters, 66% went for Democrats and 32% for Republicans.
 In 2024 House races, the margin was the same at 34 points in favor of Democrats. 
 — Alex Harring 
 50 Min Ago Ohio Senate race leans toward Democrat Sherrod Brown
 Former U.S. Sen. Sherrod Brown, a Democrat, at left, and Republican U.S. Sen. Jon Husted are U.S. Senate candidates for Ohio. Getty Images Ohio's special Senate election is leaning toward Democratic nominee Sherrod Brown, a former senator, according to CNBC's Election Desk.
 Brown is facing Republican Sen. Jon Husted, who was appointed to replace Vice President JD Vance.
 The Cook Report had rated the race a "Toss Up."
 — Garrett Downs and Dan Mangan 
 51 Min Ago Tillis congratulates Cooper after North Carolina win
 Sen. Thom Tillis speaks on CNBC's "Squawk Box" in Washington, D.C., June 3, 2026. CNBC Thom Tillis , North Carolina's retiring GOP senator of over a decade, congratulated the Democrat who just flipped his seat. 
 Democrat Roy Cooper won Tillis' seat, the AP projected. The former governor defeated Republican Michael Whatley, becoming the first North Carolina Democrat elected to the Senate since 2008. 
 "I look forward to working with him during the transition," Tillis said in an X post. "Representing the Old North State in the world's most deliberative body is an honor of a lifetime and Susan and I wish Roy and Kristin the very best in the years ahead."
 Tillis announced his retirement in June 2025 after facing attacks from Trump when he voted "no" on the president's "big beautiful bill."
 — Irit Skulnik 
 52 Min Ago Democrat Bottoms flips Georgia gubernatorial seat, defeating billionaire Jackson 
 Georgia Democratic gubernatorial candidate Keisha Lance Bottoms speaks during a campaign event at the Georgia Theater in Athens, Georgia, Sept. 13, 2026. Elijah Nouvelage | Getty Images News | Getty Images Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms will win the Georgia gubernatorial election, flipping the governorship from red to blue, the AP projected. 
 Bottoms defeated billionaire healthcare executive Rick Jackson, who defeated a crowded field in the primary and was endorsed by President Donald Trump. 
 A former mayor of Atlanta, Bottoms will be the first Black woman elected governor. Bottoms' election is the second major Democratic statewide win in Georgia on Tuesday, following Sen. Jon Ossoff's reelection. 
 — Garrett Downs 
 1 Hour Ago South Carolina Senate race is leaning toward Democrat Annie Andrews
 South Carolina Democratic Senate nominee Annie Andrews is now favored in her race against Republican Sen. Darline Graham , who was appointed to fill the rest of her brother Lindsey Graham's term after he died in July .
 The race "leans Democratic," according to CNBC's Election Desk.
 The contest was not expected to be close, as South Carolina hasn't elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1998.
 But Graham struggled to consolidate support after a bitter GOP primary in August, and Andrews, a pediatrician, closed the gap. The Cook Report shifted the rating from "likely Republican" to " Lean R " on Oct. 20.
 — Justin Papp and Dan Mangan 
 1 Hour Ago Sherrod Brown faces split electorate in quest to return to Ohio office
 Voters cast their ballots on Election Day at a polling location at the Burbank Early Childhood School in Columbus, Ohio, Nov. 3, 2026. Michael M. Santiago | Getty Images Ohio voters are split on how they feel about former Sen. Sherrod Brown, a Democrat trying to reclaim a seat he held for 18 years.
 Brown's rating was split 48%-48% between favorable and unfavorable in the CNBC Voter Poll. On his views generally, 45% rate him too extreme while 55% see him as not too extreme.
 Republican Jon Husted faces a lopsided favorability rating: Just 39% view him positively, while 53% see him unfavorably.
 — Jeff Cox 
 1 Hour Ago Democrats estimated to win at least 210 House seats, GOP still at 160: CNBC Election Desk
 Democrats' floor continues to rise in the U.S. House: They are now estimated to win a minimum of 210 seats when all races are decided, versus at least 160 seats for Republicans, CNBC's Election Desk projects. A party needs at least 218 seats to control the House.
 About 20 minutes earlier, the Election Desk projected Democrats would win at least 205 seats in the House. Republicans' projected minimum in the chamber has not moved.
 Control of the U.S. House still "leans Democratic," according to the Election Desk's projection.
 — Kevin Breuninger 
 1 Hour Ago Cooper takes aim at billionaires in North Carolina Senate victory speech
 Democratic US Senate candidate and former North Carolina Governor Roy Cooper speaks at an election night rally as he celebrates his victory during the US midterm elections, in Raleigh, North Carolina, US, Nov. 3, 2026. Jonathan Drake | Reuters Former Democratic Gov. Roy Cooper cast his North Carolina Senate victory Tuesday as a message to the wealthy and well-connected: "Tonight, we told Washington loud and clear that North Carolinians will always matter more than the billionaires and the insiders," he told supporters.
 The former governor built his campaign around a simple promise to " make stuff cost less ," tapping into frustration among families struggling with grocery bills, farmers facing rising costs and small businesses hurt by tariffs.
 Pledging to be an independent voice willing to work across party lines, Cooper called for a course correction in Washington. "I am still a prisoner of hope," he said.
 Cooper will win the Senate race on Tuesday, the AP projects, defeating Republican Michael Whatley and flipping the seat.
 — Luke Fountain 
 1 Hour Ago Republican Byron Donalds elected Florida governor, AP projects
 GOP gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds attends a midterm campaign rally in Lakeland, Florida, US, Oct. 1, 2026. Kevin Lamarque | Reuters Rep. Byron Donalds will win the Florida gubernatorial race, keeping Tallahassee in Republican hands, the AP has projected. 
 Donalds defeated former Republican Rep. David Jolly, who was running as a Democrat. 
 Donalds' victory is a win for Trump, who endorsed Donalds early in the Republican primary, and staves off a Republican worst-case scenario where the GOP loses ground in the Sunshine State. 
 — Garrett Downs 
 1 Hour Ago Ken Paxton has high negatives in Texas Senate race
 Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, a Republican candidate for the U.S. Senate, speaks to attendees during a campaign rally at Matt's Rancho Martinez in Allen, Texas, May 19, 2026. Elías Valverde II | The Dallas Morning News | Getty Images Republican Ken Paxton will have to overcome negative voter perceptions if he's going to win the Texas Senate race, even with the war chest Elon Musk has deployed.
 Paxton is viewed negatively by 61% of the electorate, the CNBC Voter Poll found, with just 35% positive. Similarly, 65% said Paxton lacks the character to hold office.
 On the Democratic side, James Talarico has a 50% favorable rating against 46% unfavorable. On the question of whether Talarico's views are too extreme, 48% said yes, while 51% said no.
 — Jeff Cox 
 1 Hour Ago Trump has no public events on Wednesday's schedule
 Trump is not slated to appear in public on the day after Election Day, according to the White House press schedule released Tuesday night.
 Trump is set to participate in "Executive Time" starting at 8 a.m. ET on Wednesday, followed by four unspecified policy meetings stretching from 11 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.
 All of the events are listed as "Closed Press," the schedule says.
 — Kevin Breuninger 
 1 Hour Ago Democrat Pia Dandiya wins in Florida's 22nd District
 Pia Dandiya is the Democratic congressional candidate for Florida's 22nd District. Courtesy: Pia Dandiya campaign Democrat Pia Dandiya won election to Florida's 22nd Congressional District, the AP projects, defeating Republican businessman and Marine veteran Casey Askar in a closely watched race.
 Dandiya, a former teacher and principal who served as a White House Fellow before working at Apple , won in a newly redrawn district that Trump would have carried by roughly 10.5 percentage points in 2024.
 The seat opened after Democratic Rep. Lois Frankel moved to a neighboring district following Florida's redistricting.
 — Luke Fountain 
 1 Hour Ago LGBT voters back Democrats in large numbers, CNBC Voter Poll shows
 U.S. Rep. Chris Pappas, New Hampshire Democratic Senate candidate, speaks to supporters at a canvass launch rally as he campaigns for office in Manchester, New Hampshire, Sept. 6, 2026. Joseph Prezioso | Getty Images LGBT-identifying voters broke sharply for Democrats on Tuesday as voters sent the first openly gay man to the U.S. Senate, according to the CNBC Voter Poll.
 LGBT voters nationwide supported Democrats in House races by a margin of 73 percentage points in 2026, the poll said. Of all voters polled, 8% identified as LGBT.
 In 2024 general election House races, LGBT voters backed Democrats by a margin of 56 percentage points. That year, 9% of voters identified as members of the community.
 Democrat Chris Pappas on Tuesday won the open Senate seat in New Hampshire, the Associated Press projected. When he's sworn in, Pappas will become the first openly gay male U.S. senator, according to the AP.
 — Alex Harring 
 1 Hour Ago Google defends itself after Sanders slams decision to remove search at schools that ban AI
 Gemini AI signage during the Google I/O Developers Conference in Mountain View, California, US, on Tuesday, May 19, 2026. David Paul Morris | Bloomberg | Getty Images As Americans turned their attention to the midterms on Tuesday, Google clarified its plans after a report suggested the company would block its search engine for schools that disable artificial intelligence services, prompting criticism from left-leaning politicians.
 The New York Times reported that students at schools that opt out of AI features wouldn't be able to use the company's market-leading web search starting in early 2027. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Sen. Bernie Sanders and former Federal Trade Commission Chair Lina Khan criticized the decision. 
 Google then said education clients can enable web search or Gemini AI products for students individually. But the company didn't specify whether students will be able to use Google for web search without seeing its AI Overviews that show up at the top of search result pages. Google said it would implement a new kind of student-specific AI Overview that was "better for learning," consisting of step-by-step guided learning processes, rather than immediate answers.
 — Isabel O'Brien and Jordan Novet 
 1 Hour Ago South Carolina Senate race is 'too close to call'
 South Carolina's Senate race is "too close to call," according to CNBC's Election Desk.
 Republican Sen. Darline Graham , who was appointed to fill the rest of her brother Lindsey Graham's term after he died unexpectedly in July , is facing Democratic nominee Annie Andrews.
 The contest was not expected to be close, as South Carolina hasn't elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1998.
 But Graham struggled to consolidate support after a bitter GOP primary in August, and Andrews, a pediatrician, closed the gap. The Cook Report shifted the rating from "likely Republican" to " lean R " on Oct. 20.
 — Justin Papp and Dan Mangan 
 2 Hours Ago Texas Gov. Abbott has higher negatives than opponent, CNBC poll shows
 Texas Gov. Greg Abbott speaks to the media after casting his ballot in the midterm elections outside Travis County Community Center on October 19, 2026 in Del Valle, Texas. Sergio Flores | Getty Images In the hotly contested Texas governor's race, both candidates have the same 46% favorable rating, but incumbent Greg Abbott has higher negatives.
 The CNBC Voter Poll showed that 52% of respondents have an unfavorable view of the Republican Abbott, while just 2% have no opinion. Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa has a 42% unfavorable rating, with 12% undecided.
 — Jeff Cox 
 2 Hours Ago Democrats estimated to win 205 House seats minimum, vs. 160 for GOP: CNBC Election Desk
 Democrats are now estimated to win a minimum of 205 seats in the U.S. House when all races are decided, CNBC's Election Desk projects.
 The update adds five seats to Democrats' column from the Election Desk's prior projection less than an hour earlier.
 Republicans remain estimated to win a minimum of 160 House seats, according to the desk.
 Control of the U.S. House still "leans Democratic," according to the Election Desk's projection.
 — Kevin Breuninger 
 2 Hours Ago CNBC Election Desk: Texas Senate "leans" D
 State Rep. James Talarico, Texas Democratic U.S. Senate candidate, at left, and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, the Republican U.S. Senate candidate. Getty Images The CNBC Election Desk projects that the Texas Senate race between Democratic state Rep. James Talarico and GOP Attorney General Ken Paxton "leans D" as of 9 p.m., when the state's polls closed. Talarico would be the first Democrat to win statewide in Texas since 1994. 
 — Justin Papp 
 2 Hours Ago Sununu hurt by Trump ties in New Hampshire race
 John Sununu, Republican Senate candidate from New Hampshire, and his wife Kitty during a primary election night watch party in Manchester, New Hampshire, US, on Tuesday, Sept. 8, 2026. Mel Musto | Bloomberg | Getty Images John Sununu came up short in his quest for the New Hampshire Senate, hurt by his ties to Trump.
 The CNBC Voter Poll showed 56% of the state's voters found the Republican aligned too closely with Trump — a trend that repeated itself in multiple Senate races Tuesday. 
 Respondents gave victorious Democratic candidate Chris Pappas a 49%-47% favorability margin.
 — Jeff Cox 
 2 Hours Ago Democrat Jamie Ager wins in North Carolina's 11th District, another pickup for Dems
 Jamie Ager, Democratic candidate for North Carolina's 11th Congressional District, in Fairview, North Carolina, Aug. 11, 2025. Matt Kelley | AP Democrat Jamie Ager is projected to win election to North Carolina's 11th Congressional District on Tuesday, according to the AP, defeating Republican state Rep. Jennifer Balkcom and flipping a Republican-held House seat.
 Ager, a western North Carolina farmer and businessman, won in a district that Trump carried by roughly 9.5 percentage points in 2024.
 The seat became an unexpected Democratic pickup opportunity after Republican Rep. Chuck Edwards dropped his reelection bid following a House Ethics Committee investigation that resulted in a recommendation that he be censured. Balkcom was selected to replace Edwards on the ballot.
 — Luke Fountain 
 2 Hours Ago 17% of voters identify as democratic socialists, CNBC Voter Poll shows
 Democratic Socialists of America counter protesters hold signs and flags as they march, protesting an alt-right rally on August 5, 2018 in downtown Berkeley, California. Getty Images Nearly 1 out of 5 voters nationwide identifies as a democratic socialist, according to the CNBC Voter Poll.
 When asked if they considered themselves a democratic socialist, 17% responded yes. Of those respondents, 97% said they were supporting Democratic candidates.
 Voting was more mixed among the 82% that said they did not identify as democratic socialists. In this group, 53% said they backed Republicans, while 43% reported selecting Democrats.
 — Alex Harring 
 2 Hours Ago Republican Sen. Ashley Moody projected to win Florida Senate special election
 Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Fla., takes her seat before the start of the Senate Judiciary Committee hearing on "Oversight of Jack Smith's Abuse of Authority and the Targeting of Republicans and Related Matters" in the Hart Senate Office Building on Tuesday, September 29, 2026. Bill Clark | Cq-roll Call, Inc. | Getty Images Incumbent Republican Sen. Ashley Moody is projected to win Florida's special Senate election, according to The Associated Press. 
 Moody is facing Democrat Angie Nixon.
 — Dan Mangan 
 2 Hours Ago Michigan voters split on whether El-Sayed is too far left
 Voters fill out their ballots at a polling location inside Wayne Community College - Eastern Campus on the final day of early voting for the midterm election in Detroit, Michigan, US, on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. Emily Elconin | Bloomberg | Getty Images Michigan voters are split when it comes to whether far-left Democrat Abdul El-Sayed is too extreme, while considering his opponent too closely aligned with Trump.
 In the CNBC Voter Poll, 49% answered yes when asked whether El-Sayed's views were too extreme, while 51% said no. For his Republican opponent, 62% said Rogers is too supportive of the president. 
 The two are looking to replace retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters.
 — Jeff Cox 
 2 Hours Ago Republican Mike Collins concedes Georgia Senate race to Democrat Jon Ossoff
 Representative Mike Collins, a Republican from Georgia and US Senate candidate, during an election night event in Atlanta, Georgia, US, on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Dustin Franz | Bloomberg | Getty Images Republican Mike Collins thanked his supporters and praised Trump as he conceded the Georgia Senate race to Democratic incumbent Sen. Jon Ossoff.
 "It's been an honor, an honor and a privilege to serve under the leadership of the best president in my lifetime," Collins told a crowd of supporters.
 "The results may not be what we wanted tonight, but y'all, that's OK," he said. "I'm going to continue to serve in whatever capacity I'm afforded, and I look forward to whatever the good Lord has in store for us."
 — Kevin Breuninger 
 2 Hours Ago Susan Collins faces Trump stigma; opponent Jackson faulted for temper
 Senator Susan Collins, a Republican from Maine, speaks to members of the media while campaigning ahead of the midterm election at the Fryeburg Fair in Fryeburg, Maine, US, on Friday, Oct. 9, 2026. Graeme Sloan | Bloomberg | Getty Images Susan Collins' quest for a sixth term in the Senate could be complicated by perceived allegiance to Trump.
 The CNBC Voter Poll found that 58% of Maine respondents consider the Republican too much in line with the president. Collins is head of the powerful Appropriations Committee and is the only GOP senator from New England.
 Collins faces Democrat Troy Jackson, a former Maine Senate leader who stepped in to the race after scandals felled nominee Graham Platner in July. 
 Jackson has his own problems: 56% of respondents say he lacks the proper temperament to serve as senator. Jackson has been criticized for various outbursts and has a criminal record dating to when he was 19 involved in a physical fight with another man. Jackson also told Collins to "shut up" during a debate.
 — Jeff Cox 
 2 Hours Ago Florida Senate race leaning toward Republican incumbent Moody
 Florida's Senate race is leaning toward Republican Sen. Ashley Moody, according to CNBC's Election Desk.
 Moody is facing Democratic nominee Angie Nixon.
 — Dan Mangan 
 2 Hours Ago Democrat Roy Cooper wins North Carolina Senate race, flips seat
 Roy Cooper, former governor of North Carolina and Democratic US Senate candidate for North Carolina, speaks during a "Make Things Cost Less" campaign kickoff event at Clouds Brewing on March 4, 2026 in Raleigh, North Carolina. Al Drago | Getty Images Former Democratic Gov. Roy Cooper won North Carolina's Senate race on Tuesday, the AP projects, defeating Republican Michael Whatley and flipping a Republican-held seat in a crucial victory for Democrats seeking control of the chamber.
 Cooper, who won the governorship in both 2016 and 2020 even as Trump carried North Carolina, defeated the former Republican National Committee chairman and close Trump ally in the race to replace retiring Republican Sen. Thom Tillis . 
 The victory marks the first time Democrats have won a North Carolina Senate election since 2008. Republicans had scaled back spending in the state as Cooper maintained a polling lead heading into Election Day.
 — Luke Fountain 
 2 Hours Ago Florida GOP incumbents Luna and Salazar in tight races
 U.S. Rep. Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL), U.S. Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar (R-FL). Getty Images Two Florida House Republican incumbents, Reps. Anna Paulina Luna, of the 13th Congressional District, and Maria Elvira Salazar, of the 27th District, held leads of less than 1 percentage point soon after polls closed Tuesday and with more than 90% of votes reported in districts in which each GOP candidate was favored. 
 Democrats showed a strong early performance in Florida, as the AP projected them to win two seats — Florida's 14th and 22nd congressional districts — that were gerrymandered to favor Republicans. CNBC's Election Desk said Florida's Senate race is too close to call.
 — Justin Papp 
 2 Hours Ago Nebraska Senate race features two unpopular candidates
 Senator Pete Ricketts, a Republican from Nebraska (L), and Independent candidate for U.S. Senate Dan Osborn, of Nebraska. Getty Images The Nebraska Senate race features two candidates who aren't particularly well-liked by voters.
 Both Republican incumbent Pete Ricketts and his independent challenger, Dan Osborn, have net unfavorable views from the electorate, according to the CNBC Voter Poll. 
 In Ricketts' case, his favorable-to-unfavorable margin is 44%-54%, while for Osborn it's 45%-52%. For Ricketts, 55% of respondents said he was too close to Trump. In Osborn's case, the same percentage said he is too closely aligned with the Democrats. 
 — Jeff Cox 
 2 Hours Ago Pappas wins New Hampshire Senate race, keeping crucial state blue
 Democratic US Senate candidate for New Hampshire Chris Pappas speaks during a campaign stop in Exeter, New Hampshire on October 17, 2026. Joseph Prezioso | Afp | Getty Images Rep. Chris Pappas has won an open Senate seat in New Hampshire, defeating former Republican Sen. John Sununu, AP projected.
 Pappas' victory keeps a critical state blue for Democrats following the retirement of Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, D-N.H. 
 A moderate, Pappas focused his campaign on tackling corruption and lowering costs.
 — Garrett Downs 
 2 Hours Ago Democrat Kathy Castor wins reelection in Florida's 14th District
 Rep. Kathy Castor (D-FL) speaks during a news conference with Democratic members of the House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition on climate change on Capitol Hill on Nov. 13, 2025, in Washington, D.C. Andrew Harnik | Getty Images Democratic Rep. Kathy Castor won reelection in Florida's 14th Congressional District on Tuesday, the AP projects, defeating Republican Mike Beltran despite redistricting that transformed her Tampa-area seat into one Trump would have carried by roughly 10.5 percentage points in 2024.
 — Luke Fountain 
 2 Hours Ago Democrat Jared Moskowitz wins reelection in Florida's 25th District
 Congressman Jared Moskowitz (D-FL) speaks at a press conference in Washington, DC on Sept. 8, 2025. Nathan Posner | Anadolu | Getty Images Democratic Rep. Jared Moskowitz won reelection in Florida's 25th Congressional District on Tuesday, the AP projects, defeating Republican Scott Singer despite redistricting that shifted the seat toward Republicans. Trump would have carried the district by about 9 percentage points in 2024. 
 — Luke Fountain 
 3 Hours Ago Trump policies to blame for inflation woes, CNBC poll finds
 U.S. President Donald Trump arrives to speak during a luncheon in the Rose Garden of the White House on Oct. 15, 2026, in Washington, D.C. Kevin Dietsch | Getty Images Trump is to blame for the nation's inflation problem, according to a strong majority of voters.
 Some 62% of respondents to the CNBC Voter Poll said that inflation, which has run above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for 5½ years, is due "more because" of Trump's policies. 
 That could be trouble for Republicans, as 79% said the cost of living is causing a severe or moderate hardship. Just 21% say inflation has caused them no hardship at all, the same amount that said it was causing a severe hardship.
 — Jeff Cox 
 3 Hours Ago House control 'leans Democrat,' CNBC Election Desk projects
